angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 131,835 km at 13.98 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 71.5134 +/- 0.0215 mas (same row, RUWE 1.30): 13.98 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.1895 +/- 0.0079 solar radii from Ment et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-540 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...23M/abstract): 131,835 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.159 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Ment et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-540 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...23M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3216 +/- 83 K from Ment et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-540 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...23M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ment et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-540 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...23M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-540.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.084, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
